clue.text: Club where dope is injected into the cheese

indicators.note: something injected is pushed inside, so the dope goes within the cheese

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
a dope is a fool, an ass

explanation.surface: A drug-tampering scandal at a club, with someone spiking the cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: A BRASSIE is an old name for a wooden golf club, the two-wood; 'Club' looks like a nightclub or society.
explanation.definitionFit: The old name for a two-wood is a golfing term for a wooden-headed driver.

clue.text: Coarse material for which male beasts are responsible

parts.note: a buck is a male deer
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: Rough cloth that male animals are responsible for.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiffened coarse cloth used in bookbinding and tailoring.

clue.text: Applause is of little account, right?

parts.note: AC is the short form of account
a claim is a right

explanation.surface: Is praise of little worth, correct?
explanation.definitionFit: Enthusiastic public praise or approval.

clue.text: A Spaniard of Norse origin

indicators.note: the word Norse is the origin from which the letters are reformed

explanation.surface: A Spaniard whose ancestry is Scandinavian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of Norse origin' says the answer comes from the letters of NORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish form of address for a man, mister.

clue.text: No longer stress there's a supplement

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
stress is tension

explanation.surface: Relief from stress gives an added extra.
explanation.definitionFit: An addition or add-on is a supplement.

clue.text: She's always highly vocal!

parts.note: read as a chatty, loud woman, but highly vocal means singing in the highest voice range

explanation.surface: A woman who is forever loud and outspoken.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest female singing voice belongs to a singer whose part sits highest in a choir.

clue.text: The girl making petition is uppity at heart

indicators.note: at heart means in the centre of, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: to sue is to petition

indicators.note: in a down clue uppity means written upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: A girl making an appeal is stuck-up at heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, a pet form of Susan.

clue.text: Crooked agent engaged in organised ramp producing the magic figure

indicators.note: engaged in means held within, so one set goes inside the other
crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dishonest agent caught up in a planned swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooked' gives ENTAG from AGENT; 'organised' turns RAMP into PRAM, which takes it in.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-pointed star used as a magic symbol.

clue.text: A group of musicians on leave

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: A band of musicians on leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert or forsake is to leave.

clue.text: Shocking an old boy with a bit of play

parts.note: OB is short for old boy
a scene is part of a play

explanation.surface: An old boy shocked by part of a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecent or offensive, so shocking.

clue.text: This may well be brought down by the cast

definitions.text: This may well be brought down by the cast

parts.words: This may well be brought down by the cast
parts.note: the cast sounds like a theatre company, but it is a throw at a fairground shy where nuts are knocked off posts

explanation.surface: Something a theatre company might bring down, like a curtain or the house.
explanation.walkthrough: A coconut shy is a British fairground stall where you throw balls to knock nuts off stands.
explanation.definitionFit: At a fairground shy, a thrown ball knocks the hairy tropical nut from its stand.

clue.text: Footwear sold in pairs-and also singly

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words pairs-and also, spanning them

explanation.surface: Shoes that a shop sells by the pair but also one at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sold' and 'singly' only dress the surface; the footwear is tucked across 'pairS-AND ALSo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Open shoes with straps are a type of summer footwear.

clue.text: Back the row and put in new order

parts.note: the back is the rear
a row or line, as a mountain range

explanation.surface: Moving furniture: the back row has to be shuffled about.
explanation.definitionFit: To put things in a new order is to alter their arrangement, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Tot the French confused

parts.note: to tot up is to add
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French toddler who is muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a small child but is the verb to tot up; ADDLE as an adjective (an addle egg) means muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: Muddled in the head, as in addle-brained, a dated adjective for befuddled.

clue.text: Ophidian graduate followed by many another

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, a graduate
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
another graduate, BA, Bachelor of Arts

explanation.surface: A snake-loving graduate trailed by a crowd of fellow graduates.
explanation.walkthrough: Ophidian means snake; the mamba is a venomous African snake.
explanation.definitionFit: Ophidian means relating to snakes, and this venomous African serpent is one.

clue.text: Grant's toleration

explanation.surface: Grant's patience.
explanation.definitionFit: A grant is an allowed sum of money; toleration is allowing something, making allowances.

clue.text: One nurse can change this cover

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral

indicators.note: the letters of nurse and can change places to make a new word

explanation.surface: A hospital nurse can alter what her protection covers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' turns NURSE CAN into NSURANCE, after I for 'One'.
explanation.definitionFit: A policy that pays out against loss is financial cover.

clue.text: Reluctant to give credit

parts.note: sounds like a stingy lender, but means unwilling to believe

explanation.surface: A banker who won't lend.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubting, unwilling to believe a claim.

clue.text: Transport for patients and doctor involved in a universal cut

indicators.note: the doctor is wrapped up inside the following letters

parts.note: U is the film certificate for universal
to lance is to cut
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor

explanation.surface: Patients' transport and a doctor caught up in across-the-board cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' puts MB inside A + U + LANCE, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle that carries sick people to hospital.

clue.text: States having 'need of a mounted force

indicators.note: in a down clue mounted means going up, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: stress is force

explanation.surface: Countries in need of a mounted police force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having 'need of' only links; STRESS read upwards gives SSERTS after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare firmly is to state.

clue.text: It's bunk about class being reprimanded

indicators.note: about means round, so the bunk goes round the class

parts.note: a bunk is a bed
a rate is a class, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: A dormitory bunk wrapped around a class being told off.
explanation.definitionFit: Scolded or told off angrily.

clue.text: A Greek character thus sounds very pleasant

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
sic is Latin for thus

explanation.surface: A Greek who is thus pleasant-sounding.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the definition as 'very pleasant sounds'.
explanation.definitionFit: Melody and harmony are pleasant sounds arranged as an art.

clue.text: Peculiarly English hair-style for women

indicators.note: peculiarly means oddly, so the letters are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: A distinctly English women's haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A short tapered bob, a women's haircut popular in the 1920s.

clue.text: Volume that affords satisfaction

explanation.surface: A book that gives pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: The volume or capacity of something; feeling pleased and at ease.

clue.text: The natural growth of street fighting reversed

indicators.note: the word for fighting is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: fighting is war

explanation.surface: Natural growth along a street fought over backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried cereal stalks are a natural growth of the field.

clue.text: It could be made up into a suit, though it would be a job

indicators.note: cloth made up into a suit is tailored; here the letters are refashioned

explanation.surface: A bolt of cloth that a tailor could make into a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' and 'though it would be a' only link; 'made up' signals rearranging INTO A SUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A post or position of employment is a job.

clue.text: They're not striking men

parts.note: sounds like unattractive men, but means workers who will not join a strike

explanation.surface: Men who are hardly handsome.
explanation.definitionFit: Strike-breakers who keep working during a dispute.

clue.text: Everyone at home gets exhausted

parts.note: everyone is all
in means at home

explanation.surface: Everyone at home is worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Worn out, completely tired.

clue.text: One might well circulate in such a place

definitions.text: One might well circulate in such a place

parts.words: One might well circulate in such a place
parts.note: circulate suggests mingling at a party, but it is going round a circular building

explanation.surface: A venue where guests mingle.
explanation.definitionFit: A round building, usually domed, where walking about means going in a circle.

clue.text: A city company records gaining a couple of points

parts.note: a log records events
N and E, two compass points

explanation.surface: A city firm's records gaining a couple of points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gaining' joins LOG to the two compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: A German city on the Rhine, famous for its scented water.

clue.text: Melancholy Danes treated on board

indicators.note: on board means inside the ship, so the letters go within

parts.note: on board a ship: SS, steamship

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Gloomy Danes being looked after aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' turns DANES into ADNES, placed inside SS, the steamship that 'on board' points to.
explanation.definitionFit: Melancholy is sorrow or low spirits.

clue.text: Mid evening in the days before Easter can be quite mild

indicators.note: the middle part goes inside the period

parts.note: Lent is the forty days before Easter

indicators.note: mid takes the central letters of the word evening

explanation.surface: A mid-evening during Lent can be mild weather.
explanation.walkthrough: ENI, the middle three letters of 'evening', goes inside LENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Merciful and easy-going, the opposite of harsh.
